title: Rav Chinena of Vardan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (It is a place-name, mentioned in Eruvin 49a and Gittin 41a.) Hyman mentions him once, in [Gittin 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.64b.11-14), raising an objection against the words of Rav Chisda and Rav Yehudah, and Rav Chisda said: “Vardan has fallen silent” ([Rashi on “fell silent”](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Gittin.64b.14.1) explains: he was struck dumb and gave no reply to this answer).[^2]

notes.text: The supplied compressed expression is translated as raising an objection. Named Davidson Gittin 64b has Rav Chinena of Vardan raising the objection and then the Vardan/Chisda exchange. Hyman’s “only once” observation remains attributed to him; no new spelling is inserted into the Hebrew.

[Rashi’s place-name gloss](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Gittin.64b.11.1) calls him a man of Vardania. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1440&lang=en) likewise gives a place-name and cites Chisda’s reply. Hyman’s separate Eruvin and Gittin locators are retained as supplied.
